why: Signing in (signed out, a real capture: only Steam's own words). The password field makes the screen secure, so nothing on it is hidden or reshaped, and the password stays a password. Steam gives its two fields no words of their own: each is named by the label it draws right above it (STEAM ACCOUNT NAME, PASSWORD), which then shows only as the field's name, once, secure as the screen is; the view's own words for them (Steam account name, Password) give way to Steam's, naming them only where Steam names them nowhere. Sign in, which Steam fills in its blue, is the screen's main action in the primary tone; while the fields are empty Steam draws it dimmed and offers no press, so it shows as not pressable until Steam does. Its words are the only part of it in Steam's tree, so it sits in the middle at its own width. SIGN IN, drawn large at the head of the page with no bar above it, stays in the page as the screen's title, centred as the app centres it, the largest step over the paragraph's lines (of the two heights holding as many lines where their words are drawn, the paragraph's holds more characters than the labels'); I need help signing in, a link inset evenly inside its row, and the paragraph under Don't have a Steam account? are centred (a recapture with where its texts' words sit).
